problem: All VLN benchmarks (R2R, Touchdown) contain only English instructions, so agents cannot serve non-English speakers, and collecting large-scale instructions for every language is impractical. Translation-only baselines (train on MT data or test on MT data) suffer from translation errors and distribution mismatch with human instructions.
motivation: There are thousands of languages, so an agent should transfer from a rich source language (English) to a target language with little or no target-language data. Train-with-MT and test-with-MT each have one side of 'golden' human data, which suggests combining both could offset each one's weakness.
key_idea: Encode a human instruction and its machine-translated counterpart with a shared multilingual transformer (XLM-R) and decoder, and let a learned 'cross-lingual instructor' softmax gate dynamically weight the two languages' hidden states at every step.
insight: Human-annotated and MT instructions have different distributions (annotations have more nouns/verbs, fewer sentences), so train-with-MT lags train-with-AN (SPL 21.5 vs 23.9 unseen). Fusing both views with learned per-step trust closes most of that gap zero-shot (XLI SPL 23.4 vs 23.9). Pretrained multilingual encoders (M-BERT, XLM-R) clearly beat an LSTM trained from scratch. The case study shows the gate trusts the human-annotated Chinese, whose attention is sharper than that on the MT English.
method: XL-R2R dataset: adds 3 Mandarin instructions per R2R trajectory (17,394 instructions in total, 5,798 trajectories, 25 crowd workers) and keeps the R2R splits of 4,675 train / 340 val-seen / 783 val-unseen.
Cross-lingual transformer encoder: XLM-R base (pretrained on 100 languages) encodes both the source and target instruction into contextual embeddings and a pooled first-token state.

Panoramic decoder: an LSTM with visual attention over 36 ResNet-152 view features and the previous action embedding, initialised with the pooled encoder state, plus textual attention over the instruction. It yields h_t per language and is shared across languages.

MT pairing: a production MT system translates English training instructions into Chinese for training, and translates Chinese test instructions into English at test time, so each sample has a human instruction plus an MT pair.

Cross-lingual language instructor (XLI): a softmax layer over the concatenated h_t^S and h_t^T outputs alpha_t, and the fused state is alpha_t*h^S + (1-alpha_t)*h^T. It is trained with the cross-entropy over actions (teacher-forced).
Training: Adam with lr 1e-5 on the encoder and 1e-4 on the decoder, batch size 100, 10k iterations, checkpoint chosen by best val-unseen SPL, max 10 actions per episode.

setting.backbone: XLM-RoBERTa-base encoder (fine-tuned) + LSTM decoder with attention, ResNet-152 features (trained end-to-end on R2R/XL-R2R)
setting.model_size: XLM-R base (~270M params, not stated in the paper); encoder hidden size 768, decoder 512
setting.training_data: R2R English instructions plus MT Chinese translations (zero-shot); optionally a varying percentage (0-100%) of human Chinese annotations from XL-R2R (17,394 instructions in total)
setting.observation: monocular RGB panoramic views (36 views) with ResNet-152 features

results: Zero-shot XLI reaches SR 30.9 / SPL 23.4 on Chinese val-unseen, beating train-w/-MT (SR 28.9 / SPL 21.5) and test-w/-MT (SR 27.9 / SPL 20.4), and nearly matching a model trained with 100% human Chinese (SR 31.4 / SPL 23.9). With 20% Chinese annotations it already surpasses the 100% annotated baseline. On the R2R English test server, XLI (100%) gets SR 33.0 / SPL 25.2 vs 30.6 / 24.1 for train-w/-an.
limitations: Only Chinese-English, with a simple base architecture (no speaker/augmentation/RL tricks), and absolute performance is low (SR ~31%).
Requires a production MT system at both training and test time, and doubles the encoding/decoding cost.
Zero-shot gains over train-w/-MT are modest (about 2 SR points), and the transfer results are shown only in figures.
